purpose: post-hoc ADAPTIVE white-box attacker addendum: the attacker is granted each defended cell's ACTUAL trained defense checkpoint and optimizes candidate token sequences straight through the TRUE training-phase transform end-to-end (no decode pipeline); a strictly stronger, clearly labeled access condition, reported as a separate tier
budget_mapping: steps_per_wire = sipit_steps (the sweep's SIPIT step count): joint full-sequence Adam steps through the true encoder per wire, plus one vocabulary-wide snap readout
limits: adaptive white-box recovery is a strictly stronger access measurement; it does not constrain black-box recovery of the same wire, nor the reverse
the addendum reuses the base cells' captured wires, canonical truth and utility; nothing about victim training is re-run
the arm's steps-per-wire budget is matched to the sweep's SIPIT step count, but it is spent as full-sequence encoder-side gradient steps (SIPIT spends the same count per token position at the head)

not_evaluable.reason: tb-cotrain co-trains the encoder DURING victim finetuning (splitbench interleaves a minimax encoder update every tb_cotrain_interval steps), but only the FINAL co-trained encoder checkpoint is saved. The base sweep captures training-phase fwd wires only, so every capture was produced by an EARLIER encoder version than the saved checkpoint and no post-training/inference capture exists for which the saved checkpoint is the authoritative encoder. Evaluating these captures against the final checkpoint would silently attack with a mismatched encoder, so the cell is NOT_EVALUABLE. A future capture rig that stores per-update encoder versions (or post-training inference captures) can lift this exclusion.
